column1: # Reference engines for rating.sh -- S087, DEC-068, DEC-069.
# The binaries are NOT in this repository and never will be. This file is the
# record of which build each result was played against; an opponent binary is a
# measurement instrument and an unidentifiable one contaminates the result.
# uci_name must be exactly what the binary answers to `uci` with `id name`.
# rating.sh asks every engine before it plays a game and refuses the run on a
# mismatch. That check exists because the first install of the original set put
# the Rustic workspace development build (`engine 3.99.36`) at /usr/games/rustic
# instead of the alpha-3.0.6 tag build, which is a different file.
# ccrl_name must be exactly the CCRL Blitz list entry without its " 64-bit"
# suffix. tools/ccrl_rating.py reads the anchor from the list at run time and
# exits non-zero if the name is not there.
# THIS IS THE SECOND SET. The first -- Leorik 1.0 (2102), Blunder 5.0.0 (2017),
# Rustic Alpha 3.0.6 -- failed the bracketing gate on 2026-08-18: chesso scored
# 90.4 % against the strongest of them, which is not "meaningfully below 90 %",
# so every score sat in the tail of the logistic curve. Evidence in
# adocs/data/S087_bracket1.pgn. Rustic is out of the set at any tag; its
# strongest rated build is Alpha 3.0.0 at 1792.
# Blunder is built from source, in git worktrees off /home/max/ws/blunder.
# Leorik is the project's official linux-x64 release binary: this machine has no
# .NET SDK (~/.dotnet holds only corefx), and CLAUDE.md forbids the agent adding
# a dependency on its own. A .NET self-contained publish targets a baseline
# rather than the host microarchitecture, so the "compile from source where
# practical" concern is weaker here than it would be for a C++ engine. DEC-069.
# uci_name
